title: Paloma and the Bakery
premise: Paloma Reyes, who inherited her grandmother's failing seaside bakery, has spent eleven years hiding from the letter she never mailed to Isandro Eriksen, the lighthouse keeper's granddaughter-turned-novelist who left town after one summer that changed everything. When a storm-damaged mail sack finally delivers Paloma's lost letter, Isandro returns under a pseudonym to research a novel, determined to keep her heart 'trainable, containable' and her identity secret. As flour dust and salt air rekindle what they once had, Isandro must choose between exposing herself—and losing the anonymity she built her survival on—or letting Paloma slip away again while the bakery, and the town's last piece of her grandmother's legacy, is sold out from under them. In the end, Isandro publishes the novel under her real name with Paloma's letter as its final page, and they reopen the bakery together on the cliff above the light.
about_author: C. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded pre-dawn ovens for pre-dawn pages after twenty years of feeding a coastal fishing town. They write love stories set where the sea keeps everyone honest.

chapters.title: Salt in the Proofing Drawer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Eleven years after her grandmother's death, Paloma runs the struggling bakery alone, rationing flour and feelings alike. A storm knocks out power and threatens the building with sale. Emotional beat: weary endurance, the quiet terror of losing the last thing that remembers her.

chapters.title: The Mail Sack
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A postal worker recovering storm debris delivers a water-stained letter postmarked eleven years ago—Isandro's own words, returned at last. She reads it in her city apartment and realizes the heart she trained into stillness was only ever waiting. Beat: shock cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: A Stranger Orders Rye
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A guarded newcomer takes the cottage above the lighthouse and becomes the bakery's quietest regular, asking odd questions about the town's history. Paloma feels seen in a way that frightens her. Beat: wary curiosity blooming into dangerous comfort.

chapters.title: What the Light Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Researching her novel, Isandro interviews townsfolk and discovers the bakery is slated for auction by a developer who once bought her family's land too. She begins drafting an exposé disguised as fiction. Beat: purpose sharpening into obsession; duty and desire entangling.

chapters.title: Lemon Curd, Confession-Adjacent
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A late night of recipe-testing dissolves into almost-confessions; both nearly speak the past aloud and retreat. Paloma finds Isandro's notebook and glimpses her own name in it. Beat: intimacy at its peak, trust beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The developer posts the auction date—three weeks out. Paloma, desperate, accepts his offer to cater his campaign dinner, compromising her principles for survival. Beat: the price of survival made literal; self-betrayal dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Chapters She Wasn't Meant to Read
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Paloma confronts Isandro with the manuscript: she knows who the novelist is, and knows the book ends with their summer. Feeling surveilled rather than loved, Paloma orders her out. Beat: betrayal; the cost of loving someone who turned your life into material.

chapters.title: Power Outage
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the developer's gala, Isandro publicly exposes his forged easement documents, torching her anonymity and her manuscript deal in one move. Power corrupts him; truth costs her everything but buys the town time. Beat: climax of sacrifice—duty fulfilled, love seemingly forfeit.

chapters.title: The Last Batch Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Auction day dawns; the sale collapses, but Paloma learns Isandro used her advance money to quietly buy the building's debt and forgive it. She finds Isandro at the lighthouse, packing to leave forever. Beat: reckoning—anger giving way to the question beneath it.

chapters.title: Paloma and the Bakery
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Isandro offers not explanations but the whole heart: the published novel, Paloma's letter as its final page, her real name on the cover. Paloma answers by lighting the ovens. They reopen together as the fog lifts off the water. Beat: resolution—love chosen over safety, legacy continued.
